project.name: Notion2Loop
project.problem: Organizations interested in Microsoft Loop lack a high-fidelity path for moving complex Notion workspaces, which increases switching cost and slows Loop adoption.
project.goal: Build an agent-assisted migration experience that preserves useful content, hierarchy, database semantics, links, and relationships while mapping unsupported Notion concepts to appropriate Microsoft 365 destinations.
non_goals: Pixel-perfect reproduction of the Notion user interface.
Claiming lossless migration for unsupported source or target semantics.
Depending on fragile UI automation as the only production execution path.

product_principles: Preserve semantic meaning before visual fidelity.
Use deterministic code for extraction, identity mapping, writes, retries, and validation.
Use agents only for ambiguous transformations and recommendations.
Keep a human approval boundary for lossy or high-impact transformations.
Produce an explicit migration report instead of silently dropping data.
Process enterprise data with least privilege and no unapproved external storage.
target_users: Microsoft 365 organizations evaluating a move from Notion to Loop.
Teams that need to retain interconnected project and knowledge data.

layers.name: domain
layers.responsibility: Entities, value objects, aggregates, domain services, repository interfaces, and domain events.

layers.name: application
layers.responsibility: Use cases, commands, queries, ports, orchestration, and transaction boundaries.

layers.name: infrastructure
layers.responsibility: Notion and Microsoft clients, persistence, file parsing, external adapters, and port implementations.

layers.name: presentation
layers.responsibility: CLI, HTTP, UI, browser extension, and agent-facing entry points.

code_architecture.dependency_rule: Dependencies point inward toward application and domain; domain has no outward dependencies.
code_architecture.shared_rule: Use src/shared only for genuinely cross-feature capabilities with no clear feature owner.
code_architecture.anti_pattern: Do not organize feature-owned code into repository-wide horizontal domain, service, or infrastructure folders.

inputs: Notion Markdown and CSV export directories.
A sanitized companion Notion API snapshot for stable IDs, property schemas, formulas, rollups, and relations.
pipeline: Build a deterministic canonical workspace graph.
Classify items and links as native, transformed, manual, or blocked.
Generate provider-neutral agent tasks with explicit approval and untrusted-data boundaries.
Render sanitized Loop-ready rich HTML and a local migration dashboard.
outputs: Per-item HTML previews and a visual local dashboard.
safety_boundaries: Source archive and directory ingestion is bounded by file count and byte limits.
ZIP paths are normalized and traversal paths are rejected before extraction.
Untrusted source IDs are hashed before being used as generated filenames.
Rendered content is sanitized before preview or clipboard use.
The local dashboard server is restricted to localhost and its resolved content root.

ingestion: Notion API for stable IDs, hierarchy, blocks, database schemas, property types, and relations.
Notion Markdown and CSV workspace export for page content and portable snapshots.
Notion HTML export when comments or additional visual fallback content is required.
Exported binary assets for durable image and attachment migration.

canonical_model.description: A model-neutral graph representing pages, blocks, databases, properties, assets, users, and typed edges.

planning: Dry-run manifest with expected losses and required approvals.
execution: First pass creates target containers and records source-to-target IDs.
Second pass restores internal links and relations using the ID map.
Microsoft Graph is used where supported for Lists, Planner, SharePoint, and OneDrive.
Loop content uses an internal supported action surface if available; otherwise use guided rich-content insertion with user approval.
agent_role: Recommend mappings for unsupported or ambiguous blocks.
Translate formulas or rollups into candidate Microsoft 365 implementations.
Restructure complex Notion layouts into Loop-friendly content.
Explain information loss and generate remediation suggestions.
validation: Compare source and target entity counts.
Verify internal link and relation resolution.
Track unsupported, transformed, skipped, and failed items.
Generate a final fidelity and manual-action report.

proposed_mapping_strategy.target: Microsoft Lists with links or supported components surfaced in Loop
Planner or Microsoft Lists depending on schema
SharePoint or OneDrive with references from Loop
Calculated column, Power Automate, custom component, or static snapshot with warning

known_constraints: No public supported API for bulk creation or mutation of native Loop page content was found as of the last research date.
Notion Markdown and CSV exports are lossy and cannot recreate a workspace by themselves.
Notion and Loop do not have one-to-one database, relation, view, permission, comment, or automation semantics.
Copilot in Loop cannot currently reason over an entire Loop workspace or directly update the current page.
Private or inaccessible Notion content cannot be migrated without appropriate source permissions.
candidate_success_metrics: Percentage of supported source blocks migrated without manual edits.
Percentage of internal links and relations successfully resolved.
Number and severity of silently lost items, with a target of zero silent loss.
Successful completion and resume rate for interrupted migrations.
Loop activation or continued usage after migration.
open_questions: Does an internal Loop action or content API exist, and does it support page and block creation rather than only workspace governance?
Which Microsoft 365 destination should be the default for each category of Notion database?
What fidelity threshold defines a successful MVP?
Which Notion block and property types are most common in target customer workspaces?
Can a supported Microsoft agent or computer-use surface safely execute Loop writes with audit and rollback?
What tenant, compliance, and licensing constraints apply to the intended pilot environment?
Which delivery surfaces should be used beyond the prototype CLI and static local dashboard?
